opportunity: A call argument narrower than int that the caller zero-extends (movzx edi,di) is trimmed to its narrow value, and C's integer promotion then widens the printed argument expression again: `sink(a0 * 3)` passes the untruncated product where the binary passes zext16(a0 * 3) to a callee that reads the whole register. Upstream Ghidra 12.1 prints the same `sink(param_1 * 3)`.
change_kind: strict correctness fix (no option: it only adds the conversion the binary performs)
root_cause: ActionDeadCode counts only minimalmask(nzmask) of an unlocked call input as consumed, so RDI = ZEXT(x & 0xffff) consumes 0xffff; RuleSubvarAnd's SubvariableFlow then trims the call input to the 2-byte value through tryCallPull (nothing outside the mask is consumed). ActionSetCasts' default getInputCast compares the unlocked parameter's local type (undefined2) with the argument and asks for no cast, so a sub-int arithmetic argument prints bare and C promotes it. Found with an instrumented throwaway build printing the p-code after every changing rule/action (subvar_and is the step that replaces CALL sink,RDI:8 with CALL sink,DI:2).
fix: p9_emit/kuna_truncarg.rs (narrowed_arg_cast), consulted by the default getInputCast arm when cast_standard asks for nothing: a CALL/CALLIND input narrower than sizeof(int), integer/unknown-typed and not an enum, whose slot no declared prototype type-locks, gets a cast to the unsigned integer of its width unless its promoted C value is already the zero-extension (int_promotion_type for an expression; the declared type's natural extension for a variable, load or cast; a ZEXT always). An argument already printed as a truncating SUBPIECE cast is retyped instead of double-cast (retype_truncation).

roundtrip.method: docs/features/truncarg/roundtrip/roundtrip.sh: gcc -O2 rt.c (six narrowed-argument callers), kuna decompile each, compile the C against a driver defining the callees as rt.c does, compare what the callees receive over 23 inputs spanning 0x7f..0x10000..0xffffffff

corpus_diff.method: kuna decompile-all --json, main vs fix, per-function code diff; every changed line must be an added unsigned narrow cast at a call argument (optionally replacing a signed narrow cast); any other text change or any non-code JSON field change is OTHER (classify_diff.py, breakdown.py, corpus-diff.txt)

speed.method: kuna decompile-all <bin> --json, main vs fix binaries, 15 interleaved pairs (order alternating), min and median wall ms; box carried other lanes

benchmark.typesweep: 444 slices / 10,748 functions, --baseline-only with each binary: type_match PERFECT 959 -> 959, aggregate 3037.19 -> 3037.19; per-slice rows (decisions + scores) identical in 444/444 slices (typesweep.txt)
benchmark.why_it_cannot_move: the change inserts CAST ops at ActionSetCasts, after every type and variable decision; over the 12,775-function corpus diff no JSON field other than `code` changed, so variables[] (what type_match and the arity/phantom counters read) is identical

gates.make test-stages: PARITY OK (1148/1148 assertions passed; +7 new kuna-truncarg keys, no existing key moved)

notes: Zero-extension is the right conversion for every narrowed input: the trim fires only when the dropped bits are known zero (non-aggressive tryCallPull consume test) or unread by the callee (RulePiecePathology), and the one sign-extension trim path (RuleSubvarSext aggressive_ext_trim) is off. The redundant casts are the price of deciding at the call site without the callee's prototype; a locked prototype suppresses the cast (stage assertion #7), so locking call-site prototypes from the callees' recovered ones removes them. Out of scope, recorded as a follow-up: the same trim at the promotion width (`sink64(a0 * 3)` with int a0, trimmed from RDI = ZEXT(EDI)) is converted by C with sign extension against an 8-byte callee; casting there would touch nearly every int argument on x86-64.
